title: Which hoodie fabric weight suits the way your customers wear it?
description: Compare GSM, inner surface, drape and recovery using a swatch trial and a finished hoodie. Choose the weight for the season and silhouette you have in mind.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: GSM means grams per square metre. It describes the mass of a given area of fabric. Two fabrics with the same GSM can have different thickness, stretch and surface feel. The right hoodie fabric is the one that gives your intended silhouette and remains comfortable in the situation you are designing for.

toc.text: Compare the swatches with a specific wearer in mind
Can two fabrics with the same GSM make noticeably different hoodies?
Record the choice so a reorder can match it

bodyHtml:
Compare the swatches with a specific wearer in mind

Imagine one hoodie worn under a jacket on the way to work and another worn as the outer layer of a streetwear set. Fold the swatches twice at the edge to feel what happens where the hood joins the neckline. Drape each over the same support. A fabric that hangs beautifully in a single layer can feel heavy at the back of the neck when doubled.

Look at the reverse as well as the face. French terry commonly shows loops on the inside, while a brushed sweatshirt fabric can have a raised, softer reverse. Ask to handle the actual options. The name describes part of the construction and leaves the final feel open.

Keep the comparison fair

Keep constantChange deliberatelyWhat you can learn
Garment pattern and base sizeMain body fabricWhether weight and structure alter the apparent fit
Hood shapeLining choiceHow the hood hangs and how bulky the neck seam feels
Artwork dimensionsFabric faceWhether the same graphic stays legible on both surfaces

See what happens after care

Agree on the intended care procedure for the sample. Measure identified points before and afterwards under comparable conditions. If body length changes but the zip length stays much the same, examine the closed front. Also check the rib where it meets the sleeve. Fabrics that look similar straight off the cutting table can behave differently in a finished garment.

Can two fabrics with the same GSM make noticeably different hoodies?

Yes. GSM describes mass per square metre. It does not tell you how firmly a knit holds its shape or how the inside feels next to skin. Fold both swatches into two layers to approximate a lined hood. Then hang each from the same edge and compare how the fold and fall change under their own weight.

Record the choice so a reorder can match it

Keep a labelled control swatch alongside the approved garment. Include composition, supplier reference, colour, weight and finish in the technical file. If an alternative is offered later, repeat the checks that influenced the original decision. An identical GSM on a new specification is only the start of that comparison.

When you discuss sampling with BEWE4R, describe how the hoodie will be worn and which quality matters most to you, such as a hood that holds its shape or a body that layers easily.
